target_customer: Restaurants in Mexico and Latin America
problem: Restaurants ran on disconnected POS, delivery app tablets and invoicing; Parrot unifies them in one system.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription plus payment terminal and processing

founders.name: Roberto Cebrián
founders.background_notes: YC page: self-made entrepreneur with tech expertise in hospitality and restaurants. TechCrunch says both founders had prior experience working with restaurants in Mexico.

founders.name: David Villarreal
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; bio is just Hello world.

technical_complexity.rationale: POS, delivery integrations, payment terminal and Mexican tax invoicing (CFDI) make a wide product for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: POS systems are sticky and payments add revenue, but local and global POS vendors competed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Toast expanded into Mexico per a later profile; Parrot kept growing and claims thousands of locations by 2025 (undated third party profile).

market_need_then: Restaurants in Mexico leaned on delivery apps during 2020 and needed unified order, payment and invoicing tools; Parrot soft launched in January 2021 and had over 500 paying restaurants by January 2022 per TechCrunch.

branding.domain_note: Moved from parrotsoftware.io to parrotsoftware.com.mx (301 redirect).

identity.logo: Parrot emoji used in the YC listing name
identity.mascot_or_character: Parrot bird (emoji in listing; no further description found)

branding.brand_signature: Parrot name with a parrot emoji

brand_strength.rationale: A friendly animal name but shared with a French drone company, which swamps search; no community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: Parrot started in Monterrey in April 2020, soft launched in January 2021, raised a 2.1 million dollar seed around December 2020 and a 9.5 million dollar Series A led by F Prime in January 2022, for 11.7 million total. It grew past 500 restaurants within a year and later claims thousands of locations. No layoffs, sale or later round turned up, so it reads as healthy regional growth.
notes: Seed date 2020-12 comes from the Seedtable URL and search summary; the TechCrunch seed article was not opened. Company homepage redirected and its content was not fetched. Competitors named in the 2022 TechCrunch article (Zak, Sunday, MarginEdge) are too late and not direct, and other competitor pages were undated, so the list is empty. Aggregators give conflicting totals (2.2, 9.97, 14.23 million dollars); TechCrunch's 11.7 million is used. The name origin was not found; a brand search returned the unrelated French drone maker.
